title: Seure (Lisbon) to de Fresne and Henri II, 12 and 27 Dec 1558: BnF fr. 3151 nos. 39-44

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3151 nos. 39-44 (Gallica btv1b9059865k views ~72-88); nos. 40/41 and 43/44 duplicate copies

transcription.notes: Not transcribed; about eight pages and roughly 2,000 signs by eye (NOTES).

system.summary: A homophonic symbol alphabet of about 60 signs with numeral code groups (12, 13, 23, 100), one key over six letters; not analysed.
system.notes: Observations by eye from the images, 21 Sept 2026; split from guiche1551 on 14 Oct 2026. The duplicates do not simply swap clear and cipher.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the leaves; print not searched.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Located the Seure letters in fr. 3151: six, not the one the catalogue lists (nos. 39-44; 40/41 and 43/44 duplicates).
Seure letters (nos. 39-44): ~2,000 signs, homophonic plus nomenclator, no decipherment; left open as too large for this pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): catalogue item 10 had grouped three letters in three different ciphers. La Guiche's 22-sign substitution stays in guiche1551; Noailles's Venice letter (another symbol alphabet) went to noailles1558 and Seure's six Lisbon letters (homophonic with numeral codes) to seure1558.

outcome.method_basis: Surveyed only: the six letters were located and the system described from the images, but the roughly 2,000 cipher signs were not transcribed or attacked.

gaps.detail: not transcribed; a multi-session job, then a homophonic attack on one key
